pr.body:
<!--

Thank you for sending a pull request! Here are some tips:

1. If this is your first time, please read our contribution guide at https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

2. Ensure you include and run the appropriate tests as part of your Pull Request.

3. In a new feature or configuration option, an update to the documentation is necessary. Everything related to the documentation is under the docs folder in the root of the repository.

4. If the Pull Request is a work in progress, make use of GitHub's "Draft PR" feature and mark it as such.

5. If you can not merge your Pull Request due to a merge conflict, Rebase it. This gets it in sync with the main branch.

6. Name your PR as "<FeatureArea>: Describe your change", e.g. Alerting: Prevent race condition. If it's a fix or feature relevant for the changelog describe the user impact in the title. The PR title is used to auto-generate the changelog for issues marked with the "add to changelog" label.

7. If your PR content should be added to the What's New document for the next major or minor release, add the **add to what's new** label to your PR. Note that you should add this label to the main PR that introduces the feature; do not add this label to smaller PRs for the feature.

-->

**What is this feature?**

Remove reference to DuckDB

**Why do we need this feature?**

See the blog post describing the vulnerability, for which a fix was rolled out to all Grafana versions earlier today:
https://grafana.com/blog/2024/10/17/grafana-security-release-critical-severity-fix-for-cve-2024-9264/

The full extent of our documentation around this feature seems to be here:
https://github.com/grafana/grafana/pull/81666/files#diff-16fb71b28e5b6197615abba8a07bc73d9bf75ebc60311663e1c29976de5cc9a6

All we've documented is that the feature-flag exists. That flag still exists in the codebase, so I'm tempted not to touch that documentation for now. We can always follow up with more improvements after this PR.

**Who is this feature for?**

Everyone

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**:

This moves the security fix into Grafana repo itself, now that it has been publicly announced. We need this here so we can clean up and simplify our Security-releases pipeline once again.

**Special notes for your reviewer:**

Please check that:
- [x] It works as expected from a user's perspective.
   Behaviour of this patch was already verified manually by @toddtreece. See his confirmation of this on our private slack, [here](https://raintank-corp.slack.com/archives/C07P60RBAUD/p1727902629844259?thread_ts=1727901896.911799&cid=C07P60RBAUD)
   Tested again on the Ephemeral instance here: https://ephemeral1511182194942samjewe.grafana-dev.net/d/be18gem24w2dcf/test-sql-expressions-bugfix?from=now-1h&to=now&timezone=browser
- [ ] If this is a pre-GA feature, it is behind a feature toggle.
- [ ] The docs are updated, and if this is a [notable improvement](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/contribute/release-notes/#how-to-determine-if-content-belongs-in-whats-new), it's added to our [What's New](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/contribute/release-notes/) doc.
pr.title: ServerSideExpressions: Disable SQL Expressions to prevent RCE and LFI vulnerability

raw_findings.body: Both branches return false, so the toggle lookup is dead code; worse, the condition is negated (`enabled` is true when the flag is *off*), so a future maintainer who "fixes" the dead branch by returning true will re-enable SQL expressions exactly when the toggle is disabled, silently reintroducing the disabled code path.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Dead, self-contradictory control flow that misleads reviewers and makes a future re-enable invert the intended toggle semantics.
raw_findings.impact: Both branches return false, so the toggle lookup is dead code; worse, the condition is negated (`enabled` is true when the flag is *off*), so a future maintainer who "fixes" the dead branch by returning true will re-enable SQL expressions exactly when the toggle is disabled, silently reintroducing the disabled code path.
raw_findings.root_cause: The kill-switch was implemented by adding a negated flag read whose result is never used, leaving contradictory logic in the function body.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Either drop the feature lookup entirely and make the helper `return false` with a comment explaining SQL expressions are hard-disabled, or write the correct predicate `return h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and gate it separately.
raw_findings.title: enableSqlExpressions computes an inverted flag check and discards it, always returning false
raw_findings.trigger: Any call to ReadQuery with type "sql", with or without the sqlExpressions feature toggle enabled.

raw_findings.body: The name reads as a mutating action ("enable") while the function is a read-only predicate, and passing the reader as an argument breaks the file's method-receiver convention, making the disable switch harder to find and reason about.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Maintainability/naming inconsistency that obscures the security kill-switch during future review.
raw_findings.impact: The name reads as a mutating action ("enable") while the function is a read-only predicate, and passing the reader as an argument breaks the file's method-receiver convention, making the disable switch harder to find and reason about.
raw_findings.root_cause: New helper introduced as a package-level function with an imperative name rather than a receiver method returning a boolean state.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Convert it to a predicate method, e.g. `func (h *ExpressionQueryReader) sqlExpressionsEnabled() bool`, and call `h.sqlExpressionsEnabled()` in the QueryTypeSQL case.
raw_findings.title: Disable helper is a free function with action-verb name instead of a predicate method on ExpressionQueryReader
raw_findings.trigger: Reading or extending pkg/expr/reader.go; the function takes the receiver-like `*ExpressionQueryReader` as an explicit parameter while every other state access in the file uses the `h` method receiver (e.g. `h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagRecoveryThreshold)` at line 160).

raw_findings.body: A regression that removes or inverts the guard (for example by making enableSqlExpressions return true) would compile and pass CI, silently re-enabling the vulnerable SQL expression path.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Absent coverage lets a future change silently undo the disablement.
raw_findings.impact: A regression that removes or inverts the guard (for example by making enableSqlExpressions return true) would compile and pass CI, silently re-enabling the vulnerable SQL expression path.
raw_findings.root_cause: A security-relevant guard was added without an accompanying regression test in the existing reader test table.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a table case to pkg/expr/reader_test.go that feeds a `"type": "sql"` query to `NewExpressionQueryReader(featuremgmt.WithFeatures(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions))` and asserts ReadQuery returns an error and a nil Command.
raw_findings.title: No test covers the new QueryTypeSQL rejection path in ReadQuery
raw_findings.trigger: Running `go test ./pkg/expr/...`; pkg/expr/reader_test.go contains no case with `"type": "sql"`, so the new guard is never exercised.

raw_findings.body: The identifier claims a DuckDB engine that no longer exists, and the DuckDB-specific `json_serialize_sql` command built on the following lines is now permanently unreachable dead code, contradicting the stated goal of removing DuckDB references.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Stale naming misleads maintainers about which engine executes the statement.
raw_findings.impact: The identifier claims a DuckDB engine that no longer exists, and the DuckDB-specific `json_serialize_sql` command built on the following lines is now permanently unreachable dead code, contradicting the stated goal of removing DuckDB references.
raw_findings.root_cause: The dependency swap replaced the constructor but left the DuckDB-derived identifier and command text in place.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Rename the variable to `db` (or inline the call) and either delete the now-unreachable `json_serialize_sql` command construction or add a comment stating the parser is intentionally inert.
raw_findings.title: parser.go still names the stub database `duckDB` after the DuckDB dependency was removed
raw_findings.trigger: Reading TablesList after this patch: the `github.com/scottlepp/go-duck/duck` import was deleted and `NewInMemoryDB()` now returns the local stub `*sql.DB` whose `RunCommands` always returns "not implemented".

raw_findings.body: Two same-named entry points with different receivers coexist in package `sql`, so a caller can easily reach the always-erroring stub method instead of the intended package function, and the method is dead code that lint may flag.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unused duplicated identifier increases ambiguity in the package API.
raw_findings.impact: Two same-named entry points with different receivers coexist in package `sql`, so a caller can easily reach the always-erroring stub method instead of the intended package function, and the method is dead code that lint may flag.
raw_findings.root_cause: The stub DB was written to mirror the removed go-duck API surface rather than only the methods the codebase calls.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Delete `(*DB).TablesList` from pkg/expr/sql/db.go, keeping only the methods actually referenced (`RunCommands`, `QueryFramesInto`).
raw_findings.title: Stub DB.TablesList method is unused and shadows the package-level TablesList function
raw_findings.trigger: Any caller resolving `sql.TablesList`: parser.go defines and callers use the package-level `TablesList(rawSQL string)`, while this new method on `*DB` has the same name and is never invoked anywhere in the repository.

raw_findings.body: The query fails with "sqlExpressions is not implemented" even though the toggle is advertised as enabling the feature, giving users no indication the capability was intentionally disabled and no guidance on what to do.
raw_findings.evidence: return eq, fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")
raw_findings.failure_mode: Documentation and runtime error message disagree, misleading operators about supported configuration.
raw_findings.impact: The query fails with "sqlExpressions is not implemented" even though the toggle is advertised as enabling the feature, giving users no indication the capability was intentionally disabled and no guidance on what to do.
raw_findings.root_cause: The feature was disabled in code without updating the user-facing toggle description that still promises the behavior.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Update the sqlExpressions toggle description in pkg/services/featuremgmt/registry.go (and regenerated docs) to state the feature is currently disabled, and make the returned error say the feature is disabled rather than "not implemented".

raw_findings.trigger: An operator enables the documented `sqlExpressions` toggle (registry.go: "Enables using SQL and DuckDB functions as Expressions.") and submits an `sql` expression query.

validated_findings.body: The query fails with "sqlExpressions is not implemented" even though the toggle is advertised as enabling the feature, giving users no indication the capability was intentionally disabled and no guidance on what to do.
validated_findings.evidence: return eq, fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")
validated_findings.failure_mode: Documentation and runtime error message disagree, misleading operators about supported configuration.
validated_findings.impact: The query fails with "sqlExpressions is not implemented" even though the toggle is advertised as enabling the feature, giving users no indication the capability was intentionally disabled and no guidance on what to do.
validated_findings.root_cause: The feature was disabled in code without updating the user-facing toggle description that still promises the behavior.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Update the sqlExpressions toggle description in pkg/services/featuremgmt/registry.go (and regenerated docs) to state the feature is currently disabled, and make the returned error say the feature is disabled rather than "not implemented".
validated_findings.title: Error text and sqlExpressions toggle description now contradict each other
validated_findings.trigger: An operator enables the documented `sqlExpressions` toggle (registry.go: "Enables using SQL and DuckDB functions as Expressions.") and submits an `sql` expression query.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a documentation/UX concern about error message wording vs toggle description. The code behavior is correct (feature is disabled). The error message accurately states the feature is not implemented. This is not a code defect.
